profile.heroNoteHtml: Platform bets in AI, enterprise SaaS, and growth, taken from discovery to launch, with the numbers to prove it.

jobs.highlight: Responsible AI scaled from 0 to 40+ customers and counting
bullets: Optimized AI use-case launch time from 14 weeks to 5 by modularising the AI agent (GXA) into reusable chunking, embedding, and access-flow components.
Pitched and shipped centralised SSO after discovery flagged sign-in friction as the top adoption blocker, unlocking $2M in incremental revenue.
Owned the AI roadmap for the Customer Data Platform, turning 30+ enterprise customer interviews into bets that lifted engagement 30% across 500K+ users.
Killed a fine-tuning track after evals showed retrieval drove 80% of failures, redirecting the squad to reranking and lifting containment from 20% to 41%.

Defined the consent, access-control, and audit-logging model for AI workflows, making the assistant sellable into FedRAMP and GDPR-bound enterprise accounts.
Built the AI quality framework tracking retrieval accuracy, deflection, and adoption, the org's first shared definition of a working AI feature.
Grew ARR by $3M in a single quarter by running 12 A/B tests across onboarding and pricing, lifting signup-to-paid conversion 35%.
Shipped a conversational engagement product from concept to GA for 50K+ SMB customers, driving 30% more interactions and 15% less support volume.
Rebuilt PLG onboarding after 20+ discovery interviews, lifting activation and CSAT 60%.
Sequenced the roadmap across 3 squads, turning customer and sales signal into prioritised bets and cutting sprint carry-over 25%.

skills.heading: AI PM toolkit: how I actually build
skills.intro: I work like an AI PM, not a feature manager. Discovery with users, then evals, then ship. I decide what the model should do, what it must never do, and how we know it worked. The cards below are my real stack. Tap any card to see how I use it on real work.

items.title: Evals before models
items.description: I write the test before I touch the model. Golden sets, grounding checks, containment and accuracy. At Granicus this call moved containment from 20 to 41 percent with zero fine tuning.
items.more: Tap to see my eval loop +

modal.title: Evals before models: my loop
modal.intro: I start every AI task by writing down what good looks like. No golden set, no ship. At Granicus the team wanted fine tuning. Evals showed retrieval caused 80 percent of failures, so we fixed chunking and reranking instead. Containment went from 20 to 41 percent.

steps.text: pull 200 past tickets, label the right answer and the source it must cite.
retrieval hit, grounding, refusal quality. One blended score hides the real break.
nothing ships below the bar. New misses become new evals.

items.title: Retrieval and grounding
items.description: Most wrong answers are retrieval misses, not model misses. I work chunking, embeddings, reranking and citations until the answer can prove where it came from.

modal.title: Retrieval and grounding: my method
modal.intro: Users forgive a bot that says it does not know. They never forgive a confident lie. So I treat retrieval as the product. Clean chunks, fresh embeddings, rerank, then force a citation in the answer.

steps.text: policy sized pieces with headings kept, so the answer quotes the real rule.
cheap recall, careful second pass, drop anything below threshold.
no source means no answer, just a clean handoff with context kept.

items.kicker: What the model must never do
items.title: Guardrails and safe UX
items.description: I design abstain and route flows, confidence thresholds and human review for edge cases. In regulated accounts a clean refusal beats a confident wrong answer.

modal.title: Guardrails and safe UX: the pattern
modal.intro: For regulated customers the refusal path is the feature. I set confidence bands: answer, ask one clarifying question, or refuse and route. Every refusal keeps full context so the human never starts cold.

steps.text: legal, medical and access decisions always route to a human.
plain language, why it stopped, what happens next, time estimate.
prompt, sources, score, decision. Audit trail ships with the feature.

items.title: Agents and platforms
items.description: I turn one-off demos into reusable pieces. At Granicus I split the agent into chunking, embedding and access flow parts, which cut launch time from 14 weeks to 5 and grew us from 0 to 40 plus customers.

modal.title: Agents and platforms: the split
modal.intro: One-off bots do not scale. At Granicus I broke our agent into three reusable parts: how we split content, how we find it, and who is allowed to see it. New use cases then became assembly, not rebuilds. Launch time fell from 14 weeks to 5.

steps.text: one way to split and version content.
one way to embed, rerank and cite.
one way to check consent and permission before answering.

modal.result: 0 to 40 plus enterprise customers on the same base.

items.title: Experimentation and analytics
items.description: I run growth like science. At Maropost 12 tests in a quarter added $3M ARR. Funnels, cohorts, SQL, and a log so we never retest a settled question.

modal.title: Experimentation and analytics: the playbook
modal.intro: At Maropost we ran 12 tests in a quarter and added 3M ARR. The trick was not more ideas, it was a shared log: hypothesis, metric, result, learning. Winners scaled, losers stayed dead.

steps.text: if everything changes, nothing learned.
activation, retention or revenue, picked before ship.
top 3 learnings shared, backlog reprioritised.

modal.intro: Big deals die on trust, not features. Discovery told me sign in friction blocked adoption, so I pitched centralised SSO ahead of feature work. It unlocked 2M in revenue and opened FedRAMP and GDPR accounts.

steps.text: SSO, provisioning, clean offboarding.
consent records, access checks, audit logs, residency options.
pilot tenant, admin docs, support script, rollback path.

teardowns.heading: Teardowns: how I read a product
teardowns.intro: One teardown of my own AI support work, in four parts. Each card opens the full breakdown: who it serves, where it breaks, what I would fix first and how I would measure it.

cards.title: 1. Why AI support answers fail
paragraphs: Problem: enterprise support teams drown in repetitive tickets; end users wait hours for simple answers. AI agents promise relief but hallucinate, breaking trust.
Persona: support ops lead at a 500+ seat B2B SaaS, owns CSAT and handle time, fears wrong answers more than slow answers.

cards.title: 2. Journey and competition
paragraphs: Journey: ticket arrives to bot attempts answer to low confidence to human handoff to resolution logged to bot learns (or doesn't).
Competition: Intercom Fin and Zendesk AI optimise containment; Sierra and Decagon sell accuracy + evals. Differentiator: eval-gated answers with cited sources, not raw containment.

cards.title: 3. What is unique and money
paragraphs: Unique: retrieval-grounded answers with confidence thresholds, abstain-and-route beats confident-and-wrong in regulated markets.
Monetisation: per-resolution pricing aligns cost with value; enterprise tier adds audit logs, residency, SSO.

ordered.text: block launch below containment + accuracy bars.

ordered.note: Metric: reopen rate, CSAT on bot conversations.

teardowns.outroHtml: Want this lens on your product? Reach out and I will walk you through it.

modals.title: Why AI support answers fail
paragraphs: Problem: support teams drown in repeat tickets while users wait hours for simple answers. Bots promise relief but guess, and one wrong policy answer burns more trust than ten slow ones.
Persona: support ops lead at a 500 seat B2B SaaS. Owns CSAT and handle time. Fears wrong answers more than slow answers.
Journey: ticket arrives, bot drafts, low confidence should hand off, human resolves, edge case feeds back into evals. It breaks at retrieval miss, overconfident reply, and handoff that drops context.
Fix I would ship first: eval gated launch checklist. Nothing goes live below the containment and accuracy bar. Metric: share of answers with citations plus containment.

modals.title: Journey and competition
paragraphs: Flow: ticket arrives, bot tries, low confidence hands to human, resolution gets logged, bot should learn. Most bots skip the last step.
Competition: Intercom Fin and Zendesk AI push containment. Sierra and Decagon sell accuracy plus evals. My read: eval gated answers with cited sources beat raw containment in regulated markets.

modals.title: What is unique and money
paragraphs: Unique: grounded answers with confidence bands. Abstain and route beats confident and wrong where compliance matters.
Money: per resolution pricing fits value. Enterprise tier adds audit logs, residency and SSO. Pilot on low risk intents, expand only as evals pass.

steps.text: High impact, low effort. Block launch below the bar.
steps.note: Metric: cited answer share and containment.

steps.text: High impact, medium effort. Show confidence, route cleanly.
Agents review edge cases weekly and each becomes an eval.
steps.note: Metric: eval pass rate week over week.

builds.heading: From problem to shipped: experiment tracker
builds.intro: A no-code build I shipped using the same loop I run at work, identify the pain, prioritise by impact and effort, design the flow, launch small, and measure. Born from my Maropost experimentation playbook.

cards.title: Experiment tracker for growth squads
paragraphs: Pain: experiment learnings lived in scattered docs, winners got re-tested, losers got repeated. Sizing: a squad running 12 tests/quarter loses ~2 weeks re-arguing old results.
Options considered: wiki page, spreadsheet log, lightweight tracker. Pick: tracker, highest impact (searchable memory) for lowest effort (one table + views).

steps.text: log hypothesis to define metric + sample to ship to record result to tag learnings.
one table (hypothesis, metric, result, learning) with filtered views per squad, no-code, one afternoon.
pilot with one squad, share top-3 learnings weekly; iterate on fields from feedback.
% experiments with documented learnings; repeat-test rate trending down.
